newsitem.title: FRANCE: TENNIS-GUSTAFSSON SURVIVES NET CORD CONTROVERSY.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-GUSTAFSSON SURVIVES NET CORD CONTROVERSY.

text.p: Magnus Gustafsson ensured there would be a Swedish finalist at the Paris Open when he beat 1994 runner-up Marc Rosset 6-2 3-6 6-2 in the first quarter-final on Friday.
He also overcame a net cord controversy that upset him in the second set when the detector sounded during a rally he won and, first the umpire, then the referee ordered the point to be replayed.
"In all the years I've been playing, if there was confusion over a point, play was stopped, but here it wasn't. I was upset when they said we had to replay the point," Gustafsson said.
"We both started to play worse tennis. It destroyed the rhythm of the match."
The detector sounded several times during the set before being turned off. It was adjusted for the third.
But both players, who believe it would be better to have net cord judges, said they were against eliminating "let" calls.
"Otherwise you could get a winner from a net cord, which is not right," Gustafsson said.
Rosset said: "The ATP must have better ways to spend so much money. They should put a person there (at the net).
"Perhaps it's normal that serving at 200 kph, even if the ball passes some millimetres above the net, the vibrations would maybe make (the detector) sound off."
Gustafsson, who beat Andre Agassi in the second round, meets one of his fellow Swedes Stefan Edberg, the 1990 winner, or 12th seed Thomas Enqvist in the semifinals.
The 29-year-old, who was out of the game for a year following surgery on his right sholder, had the measure of Rosset's booming service, the fastest recorded in the Bercy tournament at 207 kph.
"I like his serve, even if it's very hard. I have more trouble with some slower serves," said Gustafsson, whose returns often surprised the Swiss.
In the fifth game of the first set when the Swiss giant double-faulted, Gustafsson broke Rosset, who had eliminated Pete Sampras on Wednesday.
The Swede broke service again in the seventh game when he answered two successive aces from Rosset with a winning retrieval at the net and wrapped up the set in half an hour.

His concentration affected in the second set, the Swede was broken in the second and eighth games. He saved three break points in the ninth game before Rosset took the set with his seventh ace of the set and 13th of the match.
Gustafsson's only two aces of the match -- to 16 from Rosset -- helped him win the third set on his first match point.
The Swede, who is on anti-inflammatory pills for his shoulder, will have X-rays after next week's Stockholm tournament to determine whether he needs more surgery.
